SB-01.c01: More students die **getting on and off** a school bus each year than **riding inside** one, so most of this lesson is about the bus stop.
A **CLP** holder with a P and/or S endorsement may **not** carry passengers; only auditors, inspectors, test examiners, other trainees, and the accompanying CDL holder may ride.
[CA] Parents, guardians, and chartering parties may not put a child **at least 8 but under 16** on a bus unless the child is properly buckled.
A **danger zone** is the area on every side of the bus where a child is most likely to be hit, by another car or the bus itself.
**Amber** lights flash **before** the stop to warn drivers; **red** lights flash **while** the bus is stopped for students, and traffic must stop.
SB-01.c02: The danger zone in front can reach **30 ft** from the bumper; the **first 12 ft** is the most dangerous part.
The danger zones reach **12 ft** from the left side, the right side, and behind the rear bumper.
The whole area to the **left** of the bus is **always dangerous** because of passing cars.
These are the places where children are most likely to be hit, by passing traffic or by their own bus.
SB-01.c03: **Check every mirror before you drive**, and get any wrong mirror adjusted; the mirrors are how you watch the danger zones.
Flat mirrors sit on both front corners and show traffic, clearances, and students **along the sides and behind** the bus.
Adjust them to see **200 ft, or 4 bus lengths**, behind the bus, along the sides, and the **rear tires** touching the ground.
Blind spots: below and in front of each mirror, and behind the rear bumper, running **50 to 150 ft** back and up to **400 ft** on a long, wide bus.
SB-01.c04: Convex mirrors sit **below** the flat mirrors and show the sides at a **wide angle**: traffic, clearances, and students beside the bus.
People and objects do **not** look their true size or distance in convex mirrors.
Adjust them to see the **entire side** up to the mirror mounts, the front of the rear tires, and **at least 1 traffic lane** on each side.
SB-01.c05: Crossview mirrors on the left and right **front corners** show the **front bumper danger zone**, the service door, and the front wheel area.
They do **not** show true size and distance, and the **driver** must make sure they are adjusted.
[CA] California regulations (CCR Title 13 §1258) require **every school bus** to have a crossview mirror on the front outside.
Adjust them to see the front from the **bumper at ground level** (direct and mirror views overlap), both **front tires**, and up to the **service door**.
Check the crossview, convex, and flat mirrors in a **logical order** every time, so no child is missed in any danger zone.
SB-01.c06: The overhead inside mirror sits **above the windshield** on the driver's side and is for watching **students inside** the bus.
Its blind spots are right behind the driver's seat and from the rear bumper to **400 ft or more** behind; use the outside mirrors for that traffic.
Adjust it so the **top of the rear window** is at the top of the mirror and you see **all students**, including heads right behind you.
SB-01.c07: **Never move a bus stop** without **written approval** from the right school district official.
Approach slowly, keep checking all mirrors, and turn on the **amber lights** at least **200 ft** or about **5–10 seconds** before the stop.
Turn on the **right turn signal** about **100–300 ft** or **3–5 seconds** before pulling over, and move as far right as you can.
Stop with the front bumper **at least 10 ft** from the students, so they must walk to the bus where you can see them.
Put it in **Park** (or Neutral) and **set the parking brake**; turn on the **red lights** when traffic is a safe distance away, with the stop arm out.
SB-01.c08: Students wait **facing the bus** and board only **when you signal**, slowly, in single file, using the handrail.
**Count** the students and make sure all board; don't move until they are **seated and facing forward**.
A student is missing? **Secure the bus, take the key**, and look all around and underneath the bus.
Route pull-away (**7 steps**): close door, in gear, release parking brake, red lights off, **left** signal on, check mirrors, let heavy traffic clear.
At the school campus, also **turn off the ignition**, take the key if you leave the driver's area, and stand where you can supervise.
SB-01.c09: Students stay **seated until told**; count them off and have them walk **at least 10 ft** from the side of the bus, where you can see them.
Can't account for a student? **Secure the bus, take the key**, and check around and under it; then use the same 7 pull-away steps.
Missed a student's stop? **Do not back up**; follow local procedures.
[CA] With no officer or signal controlling traffic, **escort** prekindergarten, kindergarten, and grades **1–8** across with a hand-held **STOP** sign.
[CA] Every crossing student walks **in front of the bus**, and all must be safely across before the bus moves.
SB-01.c10: School unloading rules often **differ** from route rules; secure the bus (ignition **off**, take the key if you leave) and supervise the unloading.
[CA] Escort prekindergarten, kindergarten, and grade **1–8** students who must cross the road, using the hand-held STOP sign.
**Walk through the bus** to check for hiding or sleeping students and items left behind, and make sure no one comes back to the bus.
School pull-away has **9 steps**: the route list plus **fasten your safety belt** and **start the engine**.
SB-01.c11: Watch for students who **drop out of sight**, such as a child stopping for, or running back for, a dropped object.
Teach students to **leave the dropped object**, move out of the danger zones, and **get the driver's attention**.
Clothing, accessories, or body parts caught in the **handrail or door** have hurt or killed children; watch each student reach a safe place before moving.
Post-trip, walk through and around the bus for left articles, **sleeping students**, open windows and doors, problems (mirrors, flashing lamps, stop arms), and damage.
Report any problem **right away** to your supervisor or school officials.
